sections.h2: Where is Rockville, Maryland, and what makes it different from other Montgomery County towns?
sections.html:
Rockville is the county seat of Montgomery County, Maryland, in the Piedmont region and part of the Washington metropolitan area. Three creeks cross the city: Rock Creek, Cabin John Creek and Watts Branch.

The city runs on a council-manager form of government. Monique Ashton was elected mayor in November 2023, following Bridget Donnell Newton, who served from 2013 to 2023.

Because Rockville is a city inside a county, a house here answers to two sets of rules and two tax levies. That is the main thing a seller should keep in mind.

sections.h2: How did Rockville grow, and why do some parts look older than others?
sections.html:
Land patents in the area date to the early 1700s, and Rockville was named in 1803 after Montgomery County was created in 1776. The town was incorporated in 1860, and the Baltimore and Ohio Railroad reached it in 1873.

Growth then came in layers. Twinbrook was annexed in 1949 and Congressional Airport closed in 1954. Urban renewal from the 1960s removed much of the original downtown, Rockville Mall came down in 1994, and the Town Center was renovated starting in 2004.

The result is a mix. Older blocks near the courthouse and in districts such as Rockville Park and West Montgomery Avenue sit beside mid-century subdivisions like Twinbrook and newer planned areas. Say which part of the city your house is in when you describe it.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers in and around Rockville?
sections.html:
Government and education lead the list. Rockville sits on the I-270 Technology Corridor, which includes software, biotechnology and federal institutions, and the city's 2025 annual financial report lists these top employers:

Bethesda Softworks and ZeniMax Media are headquartered in the city. The median household income in 2020 was $111,797, and the poverty rate was 7.8%, according to the Wikipedia summary of census data.

sections.h2: How do people get around Rockville?
sections.html:
Rockville is served by Metro, commuter rail and Amtrak. The Metro Red Line stops at Rockville and Twinbrook stations, both opened in 1984, and MARC's Brunswick Line serves Rockville Station on the way to Washington Union Station. Amtrak also runs from Rockville to Chicago and Washington.

  • I-270 is the main highway.
  • Maryland Route 355, known as Rockville Pike, is the main commercial road.
  • Ride On provides local and county bus service.

For a seller, house location relative to the Red Line and I-270 shapes how you describe the property. It is a fact buyers can check themselves, so state it plainly.

sections.h2: Which schools and colleges are in Rockville?
sections.html:
Montgomery County Public Schools runs the public schools. Rockville's high schools include Thomas S. Wootton, Richard Montgomery and Rockville High School.

Montgomery College has its main campus in Rockville and enrolled more than 15,000 students as of March 2019. The University of Maryland Global Campus, the Johns Hopkins Montgomery County Campus and the Universities at Shady Grove are nearby but outside city limits.

sections.h2: What is the weather like in Rockville, and what does it mean for a house?
sections.html:
Rockville has a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and mild to cool winters. Average annual precipitation from 1981 to 2010 was about 40.3 inches, and snowfall averages about 17.1 inches a year.

The recorded range is wide: a record high of 105 degrees in July and a record low of minus 13 in January. With freeze and thaw cycles and long humid stretches, roofs, gutters, attic ventilation and basement moisture are reasonable items to check before a sale. Because creeks cross the city, ask about drainage if your lot sits low.

sections.h2: What historic district rules apply to a Rockville house?
sections.html:
If the house is in a locally designated historic district, exterior changes need a Certificate of Approval from the Historic District Commission. The commission meets on the third Thursday of each month at 7 p.m.

  • Work that needs review includes additions, demolition, window and door changes, roofing and siding changes, fences, driveways and major tree removal.
  • Some minor work, such as accessory structures up to 150 square feet, can be approved by staff.
  • The city aims to schedule review within 45 days of accepting an application, and an approved project must be finished within five years.
  • Building and use permits are separate from the Certificate of Approval.

The city lists many National Register properties, including the Beall-Dawson House, Old St. Mary's Church and the Rockville Railroad Station. A national listing and a local designation are different things, so confirm which one applies to your address.

sections.h2: Do rental licenses apply when selling a Rockville house?
sections.html:
They apply if the house is rented. Rockville requires a Rental Property License for the establishment or renewal of a single-family rental, which covers detached houses, townhomes and condominiums. The Community Planning and Development Services Department administers the licenses.

If tenants live in the house you plan to sell, find out whether the license is current before listing. The city's page does not list fees or inspection steps, so ask the department directly for the application and any inspection requirement.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work for a Rockville house?
sections.html:
The city's tax is billed on the Montgomery County consolidated tax bill, and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation sets assessed values. The city rate is $0.292 per $100, and the fiscal 2026 state table shows a county rate of 0.7212, a city rate of 0.2920 and a special rate of 0.2056, for a total of 1.2188.

Bills go out in July. Maryland reassesses each property every three years, and the increase is spread equally over those three years. An owner can appeal within 45 days of the notice date, first to the local assessment office, then to the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board within 30 days of the final notice, and then to the Maryland Tax Court within 30 days of the board's order.

The city's supplement to the Homeowners' Property Tax Credit is available to households with gross income up to $91,000 and net worth under $200,000, excluding the home and qualified retirement savings, on the first $495,000 of assessed value. The city Finance Department can be reached at 240-314-8400.

sections.h2: What closing costs should a Rockville seller ask about?
sections.html:
Ask the settlement company about county transfer and recordation taxes. Montgomery County's residential transfer tax ranges from 0.25% to 1% depending on the sale price, and the recordation tax has a first $100,000 exemption for a buyer's principal residence plus extra tiered amounts above $500,000, according to the state's 2026 guide on local taxing authority.

The county also runs a real property tax lien sale for unpaid bills. If back taxes are an issue, clear them or plan for them at settlement so the title company can pay them from proceeds.

faqs.q: Is Rockville, MD the county seat of Montgomery County?
faqs.a: Yes. Rockville is the county seat of Montgomery County and has been since the county was created in 1776.

faqs.q: Who bills property tax in Rockville?
faqs.a: Montgomery County bills it on one consolidated bill that includes the city's $0.292 per $100 rate. Bills are issued in July, and the State Department of Assessments and Taxation sets the assessed values.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Rockville property assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the reassessment notice. Appeals go first to the local assessment office, then to the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board within 30 days, and then to the Maryland Tax Court within 30 days.

faqs.q: Do I need city approval to change the outside of a historic Rockville house?
faqs.a: Yes, if the house is in a locally designated district. The Historic District Commission reviews exterior work such as roofing, siding, windows, fences and driveways, and it meets on the third Thursday of each month.

faqs.q: Does Rockville require a license to rent a single-family house?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires a Rental Property License for single-family rentals, including townhomes and condominiums. Contact Community Planning and Development Services for the application.
